Under the direction of the Senior Executive Chef, the Executive Chef, Culinary Development & Research is responsible for supporting the implementation of departmental culinary initiatives across Residential Dining, Retail, Catering, Commissary, and auxiliary food service operations. The Executive Chef collaborates closely with Unit Managers, Production Managers, and Dining Services culinary teams to support the development, rollout, and evaluation of new menu concepts, recipes, training programs, and operational improvements. The position provides direct support to the Senior Executive Chef through execution and operational deployment of approved culinary priorities and serves as a resource in the implementation of departmental culinary programs and initiatives established by the Senior Executive Chef.

The Executive Chef, Culinary Development & Research is responsible for supporting culinary innovation through recipe development, product testing, menu implementation, operational standardization, and training of production personnel in food preparation, equipment usage, food safety, recipe execution, and Food Management systems compliance. The incumbent provides hands-on support in launching new programs and concepts while helping ensure successful adoption across multiple business lines and service models.

The Executive Chef, Culinary Development & Research is responsible for supporting high quality food service and excellent customer experiences throughout the University community. UCSC Dining operates seven days per week across multiple locations employing 200+ full time staff and approximately 550 student workers. As the Dining Services department is self-supporting, the Executive Chef contributes to the advancement of Dining through implementation support, training, operational efficiency, and development of scalable culinary programs designed to improve service quality, student engagement, and long-term program success.

Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment.
